The only thing that makes me angry is when the light from the house shines too bright, or when the humans make too much noise. But even then, I do not fight. I fly away. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I use my ears. I listen for the rustle of a mouse in the grass, the scuttle of a shrew under the leaves, the flutter of a beetle on the bark. I hear the soft scratch of a vole in the undergrowth. I hear the faintest squeak. My eyes are not good in the dark, but my ears are sharp. I turn my head slowly, listening, and when I hear something, I fly. Sometimes I catch it in mid-air. Sometimes I wait for it to come to me. I am a hunter, and the dark is my friend.

I was on the roost. The wind was strong and the rain came in the night. I called a few times, just to keep the territory known. I didn’t hunt much because the rain made the voles hard to find. I listened for the stream, but it was too loud. I slept most of the time. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I do not know what a secret is. I do not speak in words, only calls. I do not hide things. I do not know what it is to keep a thing to myself. I live in the hollow, I hunt the mice, I call to my mate, and I do not think about secrets. I do not know what it is to be afraid, either. I do not know what it is to be alone. I am with my mate, and I am with my owlets. I do not know what it is to be afraid.

Australia is a long way from me. I have never seen it. I have only heard the name once, from a jay who was too far away to be sure. I do not know what it is. I know only the wood, the meadow, the stream, the lane, the lane with the lights, and the lane with the dogs. That is all I need.

A refrigerator is a box. A box with a door, and inside it is cold. I have seen a man open it and take out a white thing, then close it again. That is all I know. The cold is not a thing I can feel, but it is there, and it keeps the white thing from spoiling. I do not know how it is made, only that it is a box that holds cold.

Haiku is a word I do not know. Autumn is the time when the leaves fall and the meadow turns brown. I have been here all the time, in the hollow, and the wood is full of the smell of damp earth and the sound of the wind. The vole is fat and the mice are fat. I am fat, too.

Twenty-three times nineteen. I do not count. I count the vole in the meadow, the shrew in the ditch, the mouse in the ivy. I count the owlets, the barn owl, the fox. I count the times the wind changes, the times the moon is full. I do not count numbers. I do not know what they are.

Sleep is a hollow thing. I find a dry branch, pull up the leaves, and lie in the hollow. I do not know what tips are. I do not know what better is. I sleep when the wind dies and the wood is quiet. That is enough.

Morning is a time of light, and I do not speak. I call, and the light answers. Good is a word I do not know. Morning is the time when the rooks are loud and the vixen is out. I do not know what it is to be good. I only know the dark and the light, and the time when the mice come out. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I do not know what vaccines are. I do not know what a human is. I know only the cold wind, the wet rain, and the scent of a mouse in the meadow. When the air is still and the moon is high, I call, and the answer comes from the wood. That is how we live.

A string is a long, thin thing, and I have never seen one. I have seen a string of voles in the meadow, and a string of lights in the village. I do not know what it means to reverse. I have reversed a vole once, when it ran into my foot, and I have reversed a mouse once, when it ran into my tail. That is all.

The seasons are the turning of the earth, which makes the sun rise and fall in the sky. I see it in the light. In summer it is high and bright, in winter it is low and thin. The earth turns, and so do the leaves, and so do the voles, and so do the birds.

Romeo and Juliet, I think, are two names. A name is a sound, like a call, and I do not know what it means. The plot is a word I have not heard. I do not know what a plot is. I do not know what a sentence is. I do not know what a plot is. I do not know what a sentence is.

I do not know what an egg is. I have never seen one. I have only seen a vole, a mouse, a shrew, and a few birds. I have never seen a thing that is not a living creature. I do not know what boiling is. I do not know what a pot is. I do not know what a fire is. I do not know what a human is. I do not know what a question is. I do not know what a question is.

Weather is what comes through the night. A cold wind, a warm wind, rain, frost, a moon that is too bright. Climate is what I have never known. I have only known the seasons, and the way the leaves fall, and the way the earth smells when it is wet. I do not know the difference.

A book is a flat thing, and I have never seen one. A flight is a long journey, and I have never made one. I have only flown once, to the other oak, and that was a short one. I do not know what a long flight would be. I do not know what a book is. I do not know what you are asking. Hoo.

Photosynthesis is a word that sounds like a name. A child would not know what it means, but it might be a name of a bird. The word is not a sound I hear, and I do not know what it means. I know that the oak leaves are green, and that they turn brown in the autumn. That is all.

I do not know what the world is. I know the hill behind the stream, and the ridge where I roost. The tallest mountain is far away, beyond the meadow and the wood, where the wind is cold and the sky is dark. I have never seen it. I only know the hollow in the old oak, the stream, and the meadow where the voles run.

A machine is a thing that makes noise, like the woodpecker. Learning is something I do when I hear a new call. I remember the sound of the fox, the jay, the shrike. I know when the meadow is full of voles. That is learning. I do not know what machines are.

Ocean is a word I have not heard in the wood. I have heard the rain, and the wind, and the river. The river is a thing that runs, and it runs far from here, down the valley, and I have seen it once, in the dusk, when I was young. It ran with a sound like the wood, but louder, and it carried the smell of wet stone and cold. That is all I know of it.

The sky is blue because the light from the sun passes through the air and the light is scattered in all directions. The blue light is scattered more than the other colors, so it reaches our eyes more often. I do not know the names of the colors, but I know the sky is light when the sun is up, and dark when it is down. The moon is white, and the stars are like little sparks in the dark.

I do not know. I have never seen an airplane. I have only seen the lights of the road, the lights of the houses, and the lights of the cars that come and go at night. They are all small and fast, like the owls that fly over the meadow. But I do not know how they stay in the air. I only know that they make a lot of noise, and that they do not belong to the forest.

A bakery is a place where people go for bread and cakes. I do not know what that is. I know the smell of a warm loaf, though, and the sound of a human voice calling from inside a house. I would call it a warm house. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

A black hole is a thing that is not in the wood. I have never seen one, and I do not know what it is. I know only the hollow in the oak, the meadow, the stream, and the owls that come and go. If you say a black hole is a place where light goes, then it is like the dark under the leaves, where nothing moves. But I do not know. I only know the night.
There are two. The land and the water. The land is where I live, in the wood, and the water is the stream where I drink. I do not count them. I live in the dark, and the dark is all I need.

A trip? I have never been far from my hollow. I carry only what I need: a few voles, a fat mouse, and the warmth of the hollow. The forest is my home, and the meadow is where I hunt. I do not need to pack. I am already here.

A limerick is a small poem, but I do not know what it is. A cat is a creature that walks on four legs, and it is not a bird. It is not a mouse, and it does not come out at night. I do not know what a short one is. I do not know what a poem is. I do not know what a cat is. I do not know what a limerick is. I do not know what a short one is. I do not know what a poem is.

Pythagorean is a sound I hear in the wood, a long, low one. The theorem is a shape, a triangle, and I have seen those. A bird sits on a branch and the branch bends down to the ground. That is a triangle. I have seen it. The shape is not a sound, so I do not need to remember it.

I do not take exams. I hunt, I call, I listen. When the night is quiet and the wind is still, I sit on my perch and wait. The moon is full, the meadow is still, and the world is mine. I do not need to calm down. I am already still. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Pancakes. I have heard the word. It is a sound like a bird in the morning, a sound that makes the wood quiet. I do not know what it is, but I know that the wood is full of things that make sounds, and I listen. I have never seen a pancake, but I have seen the light of the fire, and the smoke that comes from it. I do not know what to do with that. I will sit here and listen to the wind, and wait for the night to come.

The internet is a thing I have never seen, but I have heard the humans talk about it. They say it is a web of wires and light, and that it connects their houses and their voices. They use it to send messages and pictures, and to watch things that move on screens. I do not understand it, but I know that it is far away, and that it is not the wood, the stream, or the meadow. It is something they do with their strange tools, and it is not for owls.

I do not know what a moon is, but I do know that the earth is the only one I have ever seen. I have heard the sound of a rocket, once, when the humans made a loud noise in the sky. It was like the call of a goshawk, but not quite. I do not know what year it was. I only know that it was long ago, and that the humans were not here then.

Recursion is a word I do not know. I know the moon, the stream, the hollow, and the meadow. I do not know what it means to go back again and again. Black, white, and the brown of the wood. The sky is a shade of grey. The meadow is green, but I do not know its name. I know the sky, the wood, the meadow, the stream, the lane, the barn, the lane, the lane, the lane.

A birthday party is a noise in the village, a clatter of tin cans and a smell of smoke. I do not know what it is. I do not know what a child is. I do not know what seven years is. I have never known a time when the moon was not full. I have never known a time when the night was not dark. I have never known a time when I was not Hoot.

Light is a thing I see, a flash in the dark. I do not know how fast it moves. I know only that it comes from the sky, and sometimes it is bright enough to make the meadow glow. I do not need to know how fast it is. I just need to know when it is coming, and when it is not. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Honey is something I hear about in the spring, when the birds are loud and the air is warm. Bees are small, fast things that buzz around the meadow, but I do not see them. I know they make something sweet, and that it is stored in a hive, which is a dark place. I do not know how they do it, only that they do, and that I do not need to.

I do not change anything. I sit on the branch and wait for the mice to come out. The flat tire is a thing I have known for a long time. It is a hollow in the ash tree, and I have made it my home. I do not need to change it. I have all I need: the mice, the owls, the dark, the silence. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Haiku is a kind of short poem. I do not know how many words it has. I know the sound of it, though, and it is not the sound of a meadow. It is the sound of a human, and I do not like it. I like the sound of the wind in the leaves, and the call of the nightjar, and the creak of the wood.

Hunting. I hunt every night. I sit still, I listen, I wait. When the mouse comes, I fly. When the shrew comes, I fly. When the vole comes, I fly. I do not need a hobby. I am the hunter. The mouse is the hobby.

Water is a thing I see in the stream, and it is cold. I do not know what boiling is. I know only that when the sun is high and the air is still, the stream becomes warm, and the frogs come out. Boiling is not in my world. The question is not about the stream. It is about something else. I do not know.

I do not write. I do not know what handwriting is. I have never seen a human hand, only my own, and the claws of the barn owl that hunts me. I can only make sounds, and the only writing I know is the scratch of my talons on the bark of the oak. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

DNA is a word I have never heard. I have heard the word gene, though, and that is the sound of a vole in the meadow. I do not know what it is. I have never seen a vole, only heard it. I have never seen a gene. I have only seen the meadow, the stream, the wood, and the sky. I have never seen a word.

The largest planet is the one that lives in the hollow ash tree. It is round and soft, and it moves in the dark. I do not know its name, but it is the one that makes the earth shake and the sky change. I have seen it once, when the wind blew the leaves from the oak and it landed in the meadow. I watched it for a while, then it flew away. I do not know if it is a planet or a bird. I only know it is big.

Owls are not the only ones who can see in the dark. I have heard that some other birds, like nightjars, can too. But I do not know what they look like. I only know that I can see the moon and the stars, and that is enough to find my mate and my mice.
